This is explicitly NOT classified as a 'good process, bad result' win just because it once led -- see processErrors below for what remains to be objectively reviewed (closing price, lineup state, starter inputs, actual run sequence) before any process verdict is reached.

processErrors.summary: Stake was $60 on a ~$630 working bankroll (~9.5%), a USER SIZING OVERRIDE of a materially smaller prior recommendation. The user cited Casey Mize being an Auburn alumnus in the conversation around this bet. Personal/team affinity must never factor into a calibrated staking model -- this is flagged as a sizing-process concern independent of the bet's outcome. A single F5 position at ~9.5% of bankroll is too large for the normal manual workflow absent explicit exceptional-edge justification.

Kalshi's redesigned UI reported only a payout multiplier (1.97x) for this execution, no cents price or displayed probability. entryPrice on the canonical bet record is therefore a flagged, non-authoritative 1/1.97 gross approximation (dataQuality=MULTIPLIER_DERIVED_ESTIMATE_UNVERIFIED) -- the raw multiplier itself is preserved verbatim in shareCardEvidence.shareCardDisplayedMultiplier as the one authoritative fact. Going forward, nightly handoffs should still try to capture a displayed probability/price alongside any multiplier when Kalshi's UI shows one.

proposedInvestigations.summary: Before classifying SD F5 9/2's process quality, independently review: archived pregame market, closing multiplier/closing contract price, confirmed lineup state, starter inputs (Casey Mize vs Brandon Williamson), the actual first-five run sequence, and whether the estimated pregame win probability and the $60 sizing were reasonable -- treating the result and the sizing decision as SEPARATE questions. Not attempted in this partial import: exact inning/hitter/run count for CIN's home run is not asserted anywhere in this repository absent verified game data.
